turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My father is seventy-nine and he had a fall last month. Are there exercises for balance?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, and they really help. Start with simple ones, like standing on one foot while holding a sturdy chair.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Holding a chair? He'd hate that.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Safety first, especially after a fall. As he gets steadier, he can hold on with just one finger.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Heel to toe walking along a hallway, and sit to stand from a chair without using his hands. Both build strength and balance.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He's quite stubborn. He thinks exercise

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Maybe frame it as staying independent rather than exercising. A tai chi class for seniors is also excellent for balance.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Tai chi might actually work. He likes calm things.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then it could be a perfect fit. Many community centers run gentle classes.
